title: Bound a generic with a trait
summary: Implement a trait and constrain a generic function to it.

scenario.briefing: A telemetry formatter calls describe on a generic type without declaring the requirement. Add the trait bound and implement the trait for the local record type.

objectives.description: Constrain a generic function with a trait bound.
Choose a standard trait bound for formatted output.
Explain static dispatch, trait objects, and coherence accurately.

hints: The generic function calls a method that T does not guarantee.
Declare the trait before the function.
Add T: Describable to the type parameter.

misconceptions.description: Calling a trait method without a trait bound.
misconceptions.testDescription: The generic function declares a Describable bound.
misconceptions.feedback: A generic T has no methods unless a bound grants them. Add T: Describable so the call is valid.

misconceptions.description: Choosing Clone when the function needs formatted output.
misconceptions.feedback: Clone copies values but does not provide formatting. std::fmt::Display is the trait for user-facing text.

misconceptions.description: Believing dyn Trait has no runtime cost.
misconceptions.feedback: A trait object dispatches through a vtable and cannot be inlined as readily as a monomorphized generic.

sections.title: Traits describe shared behavior
sections.body: A trait declares methods that types can implement. A generic function can require a trait bound, so it works for every type that provides the behavior while keeping compile-time checks. Monomorphization generates a specialized function for each concrete type.

sections.title: Static and dynamic dispatch are different tools
sections.body: A generic bound uses static dispatch and is checked at compile time. dyn Trait uses a vtable and dynamic dispatch when the concrete type is not known at compile time. Dynamic dispatch has a small runtime cost and requires an object-safe trait.

sections.title: Orphan rules keep implementations coherent
sections.body: You can implement a trait for a type when either the trait or the type is local to the crate. This prevents two crates from adding conflicting implementations for a foreign type. Default methods let a trait provide behavior that implementers can override.
